ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the target image is an upright square, with a vertical dividing line in the middle; the starting image is an upright blank square. The operation instructions show that P will “print” the blank square into a square with a horizontal midline; T will rotate the square into a diamond, indicating that each turn is 45 degrees. Reasoning: Starting from the blank square, first use P to obtain a square with a horizontal line. Then use T twice in succession, rotating 90 degrees in total, so the horizontal line becomes a vertical line, while the outer frame is still an upright square. Therefore the operation sequence to obtain the target image is PTT.

method.method_draft: Forward simulation: First read the image panels: the starting image is the plain square, the target image is the square with a vertical internal dividing line. From the operation legend, P changes a plain square into a square with a horizontal line through it, while T turns/rotates the current figure by 45 degrees. Apply P to the starting blank square to create the horizontal divider. Then apply T twice; two 45-degree turns make a 90-degree rotation, so the horizontal divider becomes vertical while the outer square is again upright. This matches the target, giving PTT.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：附图中，目标图像是一个正放的正方形，中间有一条竖直分割线；起始图像是一个正放的空白正方形。操作说明显示，P 会把空白正方形“打印”成带水平中线的正方形；T 会把正方形旋转成菱形，表示每次转动 45 度。
推理：从空白正方形开始，先用 P 得到带水平线的正方形。再连续用两次 T，总共旋转 90 度，水平线就变成竖直线，同时外框仍是正放的正方形。因此得到目标图像的操作序列是 PTT。

method.method_draft: Backward orientation analysis: Read the target image as having exactly one printed internal line, oriented vertically. Since the starting image is blank, the line must have been created by one P operation. The P example in the image shows that printing initially creates a horizontal line, not a vertical one. Therefore, after printing, the figure must be turned until the horizontal line becomes vertical. From the T example, each T is a 45-degree turn, so two T operations rotate the printed horizontal line by 90 degrees into the vertical orientation seen in the target. Thus the forward order is print first, then turn twice: PTT.
